skill.name: treatment-plans
skill.description: Generate concise medical treatment plans in LaTeX and PDF-ready formats for general medicine, rehabilitation, mental health, chronic disease care, perioperative care, and pain management.
skill.summary: Create structured medical treatment plans with templates, quality checks, timelines, and clinical planning references.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from medical terminology, Markdown code fences, LaTeX examples, and template variable names. The confirmed risks are privileged sudo installation commands and a mandatory AI image-generation workflow that could expose clinical details without a de-identification gate.

remediation.issue: Privileged TeX installation commands appear in skill documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Remove sudo examples or move them behind explicit manual approval. Prefer user-level TeX directories and non-privileged package guidance.

remediation.issue: AI-generated schematics are mandatory for clinical treatment plans.
remediation.suggestion: Make schematics optional and require de-identified prompts, user consent, and approved data handling before using any external AI workflow.

remediation.issue: Command examples can be interpreted as agent-executable steps.
remediation.suggestion: Label LaTeX, Python, and package-install commands as user-run examples unless the user explicitly requests execution.

content.value_statement: Clinical treatment plans must be concise, structured, and aligned with patient goals. This skill provides templates, checks, and references for focused medical documentation.
actual_capabilities: Drafts LaTeX treatment plans for six clinical care categories.
Copies the selected specialty template through the included generator script.
Checks completeness for required sections, SMART goals, HIPAA notices, signatures, and placeholders.
Validates goals, interventions, timelines, monitoring, safety, and regulatory elements.
Builds text timelines and optional visual timelines from treatment milestones.
Guides professional PDF formatting with included LaTeX style assets.
limitations: Does not replace clinician judgment, diagnosis, prescribing authority, or institutional review.
Requires local LaTeX and Python tools for PDF generation and validation.
Templates must be de-identified before sharing patient information.
Clinical guideline currency depends on user review and local standards.

use_cases.title: Primary Care Planning
use_cases.description: Draft chronic disease plans with goals, medications, monitoring, education, and follow-up steps.

use_cases.title: Rehabilitation Roadmaps
use_cases.description: Create therapy plans with baselines, milestones, progression criteria, precautions, and reassessment dates.

use_cases.title: Care Coordination Packets
use_cases.description: Organize multidisciplinary roles, patient education, timelines, escalation criteria, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a concise treatment plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-page treatment plan for a de-identified adult patient with [condition]. Include goals, interventions, monitoring, and follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Specialty Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using one included care category.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the [template type] format for this de-identified case: [clinical summary]. Keep the plan concise and clinically actionable.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Draft Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing treatment plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft for missing SMART goals, safety monitoring, follow-up details, and de-identification gaps: [draft text].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Team Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multidisciplinary planning across roles and timelines.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multidisciplinary plan for [complex de-identified case]. Include phased interventions, responsible roles, escalation criteria, and measurable outcomes.

output_examples.input: A clinician asks for a diabetes plan for a de-identified adult patient.
output_examples.output: A concise plan with diagnosis summary, glycemic goals, medication strategy, lifestyle actions, monitoring schedule, and follow-up milestones.

output_examples.input: A rehabilitation team needs a plan after knee surgery.
output_examples.output: A rehab plan with baseline function, therapy frequency, pain targets, mobility goals, safety precautions, and reassessment dates.

output_examples.input: A care manager wants to check whether a plan is complete.
output_examples.output: A quality review noting missing sections, unclear goals, weak monitoring, unresolved safety items, and privacy reminders.

best_practices: Use de-identified patient details before sharing drafts with any AI system.
Keep goals measurable, time-bound, and linked to specific interventions.
Verify medications, codes, and guidelines with qualified clinical sources before use.
anti_patterns: Do not paste identifiable patient information into unapproved environments.
Do not treat generated plans as final medical orders without clinician review.
Do not use broad goals without measurable targets and timelines.

faq.question: Can this skill create final medical orders?
faq.answer: No. It drafts documentation support. A qualified clinician must review and approve clinical decisions.

faq.question: Which care areas are supported?
faq.answer: It includes templates for general medicine, rehabilitation, mental health, chronic disease, perioperative care, and pain management.

faq.question: Can it generate PDF-ready documents?
faq.answer: Yes. The templates are LaTeX based and can be compiled locally with required LaTeX tools.

faq.question: Does it guarantee HIPAA compliance?
faq.answer: No. It provides de-identification guidance, but users remain responsible for privacy compliance.

faq.question: Can it validate an existing plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Included guidance and scripts can check completeness, SMART goals, monitoring, and documentation quality.

faq.question: Are clinical guidelines always current?
faq.answer: No. Users should verify recommendations against current local, specialty, and institutional standards.
